audit.whatIsWrong: Two strings say Smoke Screen 'blinds your Q autos'. It does not blind.
audit.why: Riot's Smoke Screen text: a cloud 'that reduces sight range. Enemies caught in the initial impact are dealt magic damage and have their Move Speed reduced briefly.' It costs you vision and a little movement, not your attacks. Believing it blinds you talks you out of continuing a trade you are still winning — and it is 26 seconds at rank 1, the longest cooldown in the lane, so it is the thing to bait, not to fear.
audit.corrected: Smoke Screen cuts your sight range and slows on impact; it does not stop your attacks. 26s at rank 1 — bait it.

audit.whatIsWrong: New Destiny is never mentioned, so the single cheapest way to blank his damage is absent from the page.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Attacks fire 4 bullets, which cannot pass through units.' A minion body between you and Graves eats his shotgun outright — that is a positioning answer available every wave, and it costs nothing, unlike spending Aegis Assault's 22 seconds on the same burst.
audit.corrected: Keep a minion between you and Graves — New Destiny's bullets cannot pass through units.

audit.whatIsWrong: Quickdraw is treated as a cooldown you can simply wait out, and the True Grit condition is stated loosely.
audit.why: Riot's Quickdraw text: 16/15/14/13/12, but 'Hitting enemies with basic attacks lowers the cooldown of this skill and refreshes the resistance boost', and he gains two True Grit stacks only 'if Graves dashes towards an enemy champion'. So letting him free-hit you IS what gives the dash back — the sequencing rule is to deny autos, not just to count seconds.
audit.corrected: Quickdraw is 16s at rank 1 but every basic attack he lands shortens it; deny the autos and the dash stays down.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere in either layer.
audit.why: Smoke Screen 26s at rank 1, Quickdraw 16s and refunded by autos, End of the Line 13s at 925, Collateral Damage 100s. Smoke Screen's 26s is double Shield Vault's 13s — baited, it buys two engages.
audit.corrected: Numbers added to spikes, wants, early, mid, cooldown block and interactions row.

edits.before: Graves is melee-range early, so this is your lane to seize: your level-1 point-and-click W stun lands free damage before he has his E dash to reposition, and a tapped Q reset doubles your level-2 all-in. The key is to E into his shotgun auto so the directional block eats his burst, then W-stun and Q on top of him. Dodge his Smoke Screen — standing in it blinds your Q autos and lets him kite — and never trade into him when his E is up, because he dashes out the open side of your E.
edits.after: Graves fights at short range early, so this is your lane to seize: Shield Vault's leap-stun lands free damage before Quickdraw's 16s exists, and a tapped Q doubles the level-2 all-in. Cheapest answer to his damage is a minion — New Destiny's four bullets cannot pass through units, so keep one in the line. Smoke Screen does not blind you; it cuts sight range and slows on impact, and at 26 seconds at rank 1 it is by far the cooldown worth baiting. Never trade into a Quickdraw that is up, though — he simply leaves.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 you still poke with held long-range Q, but Graves stabilizes: once his E dash is up every fight, he breaks your W gap and repositions to fire shotgun bursts you can't answer. At 6 his True Grit armor stacks and his mobility flip the duel — your Grand Starfall is built for cross-map roams, not winning this 1v1, so use R to gank other lanes rather than forcing him. Trade only when his E and Smoke Screen are both down.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 you still poke with the held Comet Spear, but Graves stabilizes: every basic attack he lands shortens Quickdraw, so a free-hitting Graves always has the dash. Deny the autos with a minion in the line and the 16s actually runs. At 6 dashing at you gives him two True Grit stacks, so Grand Starfall is a cross-map roam here. Trade only with Quickdraw and a 26s Smoke Screen both spent.

edits.after: With W-Q-E you can all-in, but Quickdraw leaves out the open side of your block — and his autos keep shortening its 16s.

notes: Two corrections a player would feel immediately. Smoke Screen does not blind — Riot's text is reduced sight range plus impact damage and a brief slow — so the page was talking you out of trades you were still winning; at 26 seconds at rank 1 it is the longest cooldown in the lane and the right thing to bait. And New Destiny's bullets 'cannot pass through units', which means a single minion body blanks his shotgun for free; that was nowhere on the page, while Aegis Assault's 22 seconds was being recommended for the same job. Quickdraw is also not a clean 16s: his basic attacks lower it, so denying autos is what keeps the dash down.
